# Hiero

> Hiero is an idiomatic .NET 10 client library for the Hedera Hashgraph public network.
> It provides async access to all Hedera network services -- cryptocurrency transfers,
> the Hedera Consensus Service (HCS), fungible tokens, NFTs, smart contracts, file
> storage, scheduled transactions, and airdrops -- through three typed client objects:
> `ConsensusClient` (gRPC, for submitting transactions and queries),
> `MirrorRestClient` (REST/JSON, for querying historical state), and
> `MirrorGrpcClient` (gRPC streaming, for real-time topic subscriptions).
> All state-changing operations follow the pattern:
> create a `*Params` object, configure a `ConsensusClient`, call the async method, receive a typed `*Receipt`.

## RULES FOR SUBMITTING TRANSACTIONS (read before writing any code that moves value)

Hedera finalises a transaction seconds after a node accepts it, sometimes longer. A client that stops
waiting before the transaction's validity ends cannot tell "failed" from "still deciding"; treating the
second as the first sends value twice or refunds a payment that happened.

1. Use the whole window. The defaults (Hiero 3.0+) do: TransactionDuration = 180 s (the network's maximum),
   RetryCount = 43, RetryDelay = 200 ms. Retries are linear (the n-th waits n x RetryDelay), so the client
   follows a receipt for RetryDelay x RetryCount x (RetryCount + 1) / 2 = 189 s. Never shorten this below
   TransactionDuration; to answer a caller sooner, wait a bounded time and answer "pending" instead.
2. Choose the TransactionId before submitting and store it: var txId = client.CreateNewTransactionId();
   then pass ctx => ctx.TransactionId = txId on that one call. It is your idempotency key, your mirror
   lookup and your expiry clock.
3. Only a receipt with Status == ResponseCode.Success is a known success.
4. TransactionException = reached consensus with a failure status: a real failure, nothing moved.
   (From a record lookup such as GetTransactionRecordAsync it means the LOOKUP failed: its Status is the
   lookup's code, not the transaction's.)
   (A node with no verdict to give raises ConsensusException instead. On Hiero 2.x it raised a
   TransactionException with Status Unknown or ReceiptNotFound instead: treat those as UNKNOWN there.)
5. PrecheckException = the node refused it, but READ THE CODE.
   Definite (nothing executed): InvalidSignature, InsufficientPayerBalance, InvalidAccountId,
   TokenNotAssociatedToAccount and other codes about the transaction itself.
   Prove nothing (outcome UNKNOWN): Unknown (e.g. refused connection), RpcError, Busy,
   PlatformTransactionNotCreated, PlatformNotActive, DuplicateTransaction, TransactionExpired.
   For payments, the safest choice is to treat every PrecheckException as UNKNOWN.
6. ConsensusException, or any other exception once the transaction may have been sent (transport failure,
   cancellation) = UNKNOWN. ConsensusException is NOT safe to retry.
7. NEVER resubmit and NEVER report "failed" on an UNKNOWN outcome: a resubmission is a new transaction with
   a new id, so the value can move twice. Report "pending" and settle it with MirrorRestClient:
   GetTransactionGroupAsync(txId), keeping records with Nonce == 0 && !IsScheduled && TransactionId == txId.
   Any Status == Success among them wins (a resend can leave a DuplicateTransaction record beside the real
   one); any other status except DuplicateTransaction is the failure. No such record means "did not
   execute" ONLY once GetLatestConsensusTimestampAsync() (the MIRROR's clock, never yours), read BEFORE
   the lookup, is past valid start + TransactionDuration + ~60 s; before that it is still pending. Send
   again, with a new id, only after the mirror says the first did not execute.
8. To see what the client sends and receives, set ctx.OnSendingRequest / ctx.OnResponseReceived.

Full rules and copyable code (classifying every ending, ResolveOutcomeAsync):
[Error handling](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/errorhandling.html).

## Getting Started

- [Installation and Hello World](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/index.html): Install via `dotnet add package Hiero`, connect to testnet, query an account balance.
- [Network configuration](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/network.html): Testnet vs mainnet endpoints, node rotation patterns.
- [NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Hiero/): Install instructions for all package managers.
- [GitHub source](https://github.com/bugbytesinc/Hiero): Source code, issue tracker, and contribution guide.

## Key Concepts

- [Client architecture](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/index.html): The three client types and when to use each.
- [Key management](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/security/keymanagement.html): Loading keys safely, async Signatory for HSM/vault, mnemonic derivation.
- [Dependency injection](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/di.html): Registering clients with IServiceCollection.
- [Error handling](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/tutorials/errorhandling.html): Did a transaction execute? What each exception proves, settling unknown outcomes on a mirror node, diagnosing.
- [EntityId](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/api/Hiero.EntityId.html): Hedera shard.realm.num addressing, key aliases, EVM addresses.
- [Endorsement and Signatory](https://hashgraph.bugbytes.com/api/Hiero.Endorsement.html): Public key / N-of-M key lists and private key signing.
